Rackstor UK Ltd delivers
an end-to-end mobile shelving engineering and project management service
designed to resolve space shortages across rail heritage, academic, healthcare,
and food science sectors. Our engagement begins with a comprehensive full site
survey and dynamic space planning consultation. Our qualified engineers carry
out structural slab load calculations, evaluate floor levelling and subfloor
conditions, survey access routes, and produce detailed 2D and 3D CAD space
designs that unlock the maximum storage volume within your available space. We
supply and build premium new high-density mobile shelving systems engineered to
match or exceed Compactus, Kardex, and Bruynzeel performance benchmarks, using
high-tensile steel shelving components, precision track rails, and ergonomic
hand-wheel mechanical reduction drives or advanced powered push-button
electronics. Every mobile shelving carriage is installed exclusively by
SEIRS-registered engineers (Shelving and Equipment Installation Registration
Scheme), guaranteeing that rail installations are flat, carriages are squared,
and all safety interfaces operate smoothly. For expanding or restructuring
organizations, we specialize in the safe dismantling, structural relocation, and
customized reconfiguration of existing mobile shelving assets, enabling seamless
moves between commercial premises or the expansion of existing static racking
into high-density roller racking. To guarantee ongoing structural integrity,
operational reliability, and statutory safety compliance, we provide
comprehensive annual safety inspections and preventative maintenance regimes in
full alignment with BS EN 15095 and PUWER 1998 standards. These regular
inspections thoroughly examine track level integrity, drive chain tension,
manual hand-wheel locks, emergency stopping mechanisms, and electronic
photo-electric presence sensors. Crucially, all installation, reconfiguration,
and maintenance activities are systematically executed with minimal disruption
to live operations, safeguarding ongoing hospital care, historic archive
preservation, and academic research.
